# Round 5 plan: invoice-extraction agent

Defaults I chose:
- New IDs assume spec.md ends at R29 and disagreements.md ends at D6. I will renumber to match the files.
- Trials per cell stay at 3 per invoice per config. I assume this matches round 4.
- The tag follows the pattern from rounds 1 to 4. It is shown here as `spe-r05`.

## Where round 4 left us

- Q hit. It was predicted at 0.91 and measured 0.93.
- R missed. It was predicted at 0.95 and measured 0.88. The naive guess of 0.90 beat my prediction for R.
- R's Why said "OCR cleanup fixes scanned totals." The wrong assumption was that cleanup is safe on every layout. It dropped line items on two-column layouts. This is r04 F9, and its fix is still open.
- The stop streak is 0 because R missed. No config is at a ceiling, so no ceiling check is needed.

## 1. Specify

| P2 | Reject for round 5. Logged as D7. | The 15 new invoices need reference fields from the AP lead, and I cannot write those. Adding tasks in the same round as a config change would also mix two causes. Q at 0.93 is not a ceiling. |
| P3 | Adopt | P trailed Q on every round 4 metric. Q runs unchanged as the reference config. P's round 4 rows stay in the log. |

| R31 | S decides the layout from the PDF alone. It skips OCR cleanup when it judges the layout two-column. | P1, r04 F9 | `layout_detect` against hand tags (code). The tool-call log shows no cleanup call on invoices S detected as two-column. |

Layout tags: I will hand-tag each of the 60 invoices as two_column or single_column from page images. The tags go in the grader-only file `spe/evals/data/layout-tags.csv`. The user can override any tag before launch.

## 2. Predict

Configs (one change each):
- Q: Sonnet 5.5 with the schema-first prompt. It is unchanged and serves as the reference.
- R: Q plus the OCR cleanup tool. It is unchanged and should reproduce F9.
- S: R plus a layout gate that skips cleanup on two-column layouts. This gate is the only change.

Every number has a band. A hit means the measured value falls inside the band.

| Metric | Q | R | S | Same as last round | Why | Grader check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Field accuracy, all 60 | 0.93 ± 0.03 | 0.88 ± 0.03 | 0.93 ± 0.03 | Q 0.93, R 0.88, S 0.88 (from its parent R) | Q and R are unchanged. On two-column invoices S follows Q's path, so the F9 loss goes away. I give S no credit for the scanned-total claim because that Why broke in round 4. | `field_match` (code) |
| Line-item recall, two_column slice | 0.92 ± 0.06 | 0.65 ± 0.15 | 0.90 ± 0.07 | From the round 4 regrade in gate 2 | F9 shows that R drops two-column line items. S should match Q there, minus a few invoices the detector gets wrong. | `line_item_recall` (code) |
| Field accuracy, single_column slice | 0.94 ± 0.03 | 0.94 ± 0.03 | 0.94 ± 0.03 | From the round 4 regrade in gate 2 | Round 4 gave no evidence that cleanup helps or hurts single-column invoices. S runs R's path on them. | `field_match` (code) |
| Layout detection accuracy | not run | not run | 0.95 ± 0.05 | None, because this is a new component | Two-column line-item tables look clearly different from single-column ones. A few mixed layouts may be misread. | `layout_detect` against hand tags (code) |

The log lines I have cover only field accuracy. Any other round 4 metric, such as PO mismatch flags, is predicted at its round 4 measured value for Q and R, with a band of ± 0.03. S is predicted at Q's value, because R's false mismatches came from dropped line items. I copy these numbers from spe/prediction-log.md into r05.yaml before I save it.

The "same as last round" values for the new slice rows come from gate 2. I record them before launch. They do not change the saved prediction.

## 3. Evaluate

The harness is `spe/evals/harness/r05-workflow.js` with `const ROUND = 5`. Every prompt reads the round from this constant.

Gates run in order. Each gate must pass before the next one starts.
1. Grader selftest. For every check, including `line_item_recall` and `layout_detect`, the oracle must pass and the empty and wrong outputs must fail. One two-column oracle case is included. I halt on any failure.
2. Control. I regrade the round 4 transcripts for Q and R with the round 5 grader. Full-set field accuracy must equal round 4 to two decimals (Q 0.93, R 0.88). I halt on a mismatch and log it as a grader failure.
3. Dry run on 3 cells. These are S on one two-column invoice, S on one single-column scanned invoice, and R on the same two-column invoice. I check that the schema is valid, that the gate behaves as R31 and R32 say, and that no trial peeked.

Then I launch the Workflow.

Workflow arguments:
- `configs`: Q, R, S
- `tasks`: the 60 round 4 task IDs, checked by hash
- `trials_per_cell`: 3
- Split cells: up to 2 extra trials when trials disagree on any field. Extra trials are capped at 90 in total.
- Budget cap: $120 hard. Any trial that would cross the cap is skipped and logged.
- Trial output schema: vendor, invoice_number, date (ISO), line_items (description, qty, unit_price, amount), total, po_mismatch flags, and layout (S only).
- Checks: code runs first. It uses normalized exact match, totals to the cent, and line items matched on amount plus description. A judge runs only for vendor name equivalence when the normalized strings differ.
- Isolation: trials cannot read spe/, the references, layout-tags.csv, or the predictions. A transcript scan voids any trial that touched them.
- The run ends with failure analysis on every miss, followed by a completeness critic.

Cost estimate (unmeasured): the run is 540 base trials plus up to 90 extra, so 630 at most. I assume about 25k input and 2k output tokens per trial. That comes to about 16M input and 1.3M output tokens. At an assumed $3 per million input and $15 per million output, the total is about $66 plus a small judge cost. Before launch I will check this against round 4's measured spend.

I halt and report on a budget cap, a leaked answer key, a failed gate, or a decision only the user can make.

## Steps after approval

Each step ends in a local commit with a plain message. Nothing is pushed.

1. Copy this plan to `spe/plans/r05.md`. Write `spe/predictions/r05.yaml` with round 5, date 2026-10-21, author "Claude, approved by the user in plan mode", configs Q, R, S, each number with its band and Why, and `same_as_last_round`. The file starts with `# Saved before the eval ran. Do not edit after the run.` I leave `r05-draft.yaml` untouched. Commit as "spe r05: predict".
2. Save the user's paste and "go again" verbatim in `spe/spec/transcripts/2026-10-21-r05.md`. Add the round 5 table and the proposal decisions to spec.md. Add D7 and D8 to disagreements.md. Write `layout-tags.csv`. Commit as "spe r05: specify".
3. Write the harness and run the three gates. Commit the harness and gate results as "spe r05: evaluate". Then launch.
4. When the completion notice arrives, close out the round.
   - Add round 5 rows to prediction-log.md, with "Which Why broke" and a plain naive-versus-prediction note.
   - Update F9's Fix line with the outcome. Add F10 onward for any new failure types.
   - Add a "Proposed for round 6" table and write `r06-draft.yaml` with `status: draft`.
   - Update spe/README.md. Commit as "spe r05: learn" and tag `spe-r05`.
